To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the Actor Search Tree Criti (ASTC) algorithm is a novel approach to solve the off-policy POMDP learning problem in healthcare; (ii) ASTC can be applied to medical decision-making tasks with high-dimensional and sparse clinical data; and (iii) the ASTC algorithm can be applied to the problem of sepsis treatment and can improve patient outcomes.

1) We have proposed a novel actor-critic algorithm for partially observable reinforcement learning, which is the first of its kind to our knowledge, and demonstrated its efficacy in the context of medical decision making; 2) We have shown that a policy learned from real ICU data can dictate dosing for vasopressors, intravenous fluids, and antibiotics for the treatment of sepsis patients in a manner that leads to the best patient survival outcomes; and 3) We have demonstrated that

we have developed a new algorithm for reinforcement learning for partially observable Markov Decision Processes, which has the ability to learn optimal policies from suboptimal data, and we applied the algorithm to a medical problem of determining the optimal treatment for patients suffering from sepsis, and found that our algorithm outperforms existing algorithms in terms of patient outcomes, and that our algorithm is robust to noise and can be used to make decisions in real-time.

the development of a novel reinforcement learning algorithm for medical decision making.
the development and evaluation of a novel algorithm for off-policy reinforcement learning in partially observable Markov domains.

the development and application of an algorithmic framework that is able to optimise the treatment plan in a patient-specific fashion, by taking into account the uncertainty in the patient's physiological states and the continuous nature of the actions.
